coverage_notes: COMPLETE COVERAGE: all 15 Ohio districts x 2 major parties = 30 nominee rows verified, zero exclusions. Every district has both a Democratic and a Republican general-election nominee, so no "no major-party opponent" cases arose. All 15 incumbents (10 R, 5 D) are seeking re-election and no seat is open. SYSTEMATIC OBSTACLE — the specified primary tracker of record was unreachable: ballotpedia.org returned empty document bodies on every WebFetch attempt (main OH-2026 House page and the May 5 Democratic primaries page), and the browser fallback failed because the Browser pane was hidden/non-compositing (screenshot timed out at 5s, javascript_tool timed out at 30s). I therefore did NOT verify any row against a live Ballotpedia page. Substitute verification, two independent sources per row: (1) the Wikipedia OH-2026 House elections article's per-district primary results tables, read as raw wikitext via the MediaWiki API — the plain article fetch truncated mid-District 9, so I pulled the section index and fetched districts 10-15 individually by section id (175/195/210/226/246/262); (2) politics1.com/oh.htm, which the contract explicitly names as an acceptable identity-verification route, supplying campaign URLs for all 30 nominees and independently corroborating every name and district. A third structural cross-check came from Ballotpedia search-result snippets (not the page itself): May 5 2026 primary, 15 seats, no open districts, "five Democrats and 10 Republicans" incumbent split, 20 contested primaries — the 10R/5D incumbent split matches my roster exactly. OH-09 (Kaptur/Merrin) and OH-15 (Carey/Leonard) additionally carry independent news race-calls. NAME SPELLING: recorded as the campaign site/politics1 spells it, which differs from congress.gov/Wikipedia formal names in six cases (Dave vs David Taylor, Jen vs Jennifer Mazzuckelli, Josh vs Joshua Kolasinski, Dave vs David Joyce, Mike vs Michael R. Turner, Emilia vs Emilia Strong Sykes); both variants are noted per row. BIOGUIDE IDs: all 15 verified against congress.gov member-page URL slugs or the unitedstates.github.io congress-legislators dataset — none from memory. Three of my priors were wrong and were corrected by verification (Shontel Brown is B001313 not B001309, Sykes is S001223 not S001222, Balderson is B001306 not B001303), which is why every id was independently checked. OFFICIAL_URL GAP: house.gov/representatives returned HTTP 403 and the congress-legislators CSV fetch truncated before the newer members, so official house.gov URLs are populated for only 7 of 15 incumbents (Beatty, Jordan, Latta, Davidson, Turner, Balderson, Joyce). The remaining 8 are left BLANK rather than guessed from the lastname.house.gov pattern, per DROP-NEVER-GUESS; this costs nothing against the contract because official_url is only mandatory when an incumbent has no findable campaign site, and all 15 incumbents have verified campaign sites. SITE SELF-IDENTIFICATION: 6 sites were fetched directly and confirmed (Conroy, Dulaney, Kirchner, Coleman, Leonard, Knickerbocker); of these, jen4oh2.com, votedulaney.org and kristinaknickerbocker.com do not state party and/or district on the homepage, so those three rows rest on politics1.com tracker linkage, which the contract permits — flagged in their notes. donleonard.net 301-redirects to donforohio.com; the canonical destination is recorded. The remaining 24 campaign URLs were not individually fetched and rest on politics1.com linkage plus name/district agreement with Wikipedia. Contract respected throughout: public pages only, no downloads, no forms, no logins, no repo writes.

COMPLETE for the requested scope: all 19 Texas districts (20-38) yielded both major-party general-election nominees, for 38 verified rows and zero exclusions. Every district in scope is genuinely two-way contested, so no "no major-party opponent" cases arose. Scope caveat: the task framing mentioned NC/IL/OH, but the stated SCOPE was Texas 20-38 only, so this tranche covers Texas exclusively. All rows sit on the new congressional map the Texas Legislature passed in Aug 2025, which the Supreme Court allowed for 2026 use on Dec 4 2025 (per Wikipedia's 2026 TX US House article); this map heavily reshuffled incumbency, and I treated incumbency conservatively — TX-21, 22, 23, 30, 32, 33, 35 and 38 are recorded with no incumbent among the nominees (Chip Roy ran for AG; Troy Nehls retired; Tony Gonzales withdrew Mar 5 2026; Crockett and Hunt ran for Senate; Colin Allred is a FORMER member, not this seat's incumbent), and Greg Casar is flagged as a sitting TX-35 member seeking the redrawn TX-37 rather than a true TX-37 incumbent. SYSTEMATIC OBSTACLES: (1) Ballotpedia — the contract's primary tracker of record — returned an empty body on every single direct fetch (main state page, per-district pages, primary pages), so I could not read it directly; I worked around this by harvesting Ballotpedia's indexed content through search snippets and by corroborating every non-obvious race with an independent news race-call (Texas Tribune, Axios, KERA, FOX4, FOX26, KVUE, KSAT, TPR, KGNS, Community Impact, The Texan, Texas Scorecard, AP wire). (2) Wikipedia's 2026 Texas House article is too large to fetch whole — raw wikitext truncated around District 9, and the sections API truncated around District 23, so section indices for D24-38 could not be read (one model-generated extrapolation of those indices proved wrong on probing and was discarded rather than trusted). Districts 20-23 are therefore sourced from Wikipedia section wikitext with full primary vote counts; districts 24-38 from Ballotpedia-via-search plus news race calls. (3) Two candidate-name spellings in politics1.com are wrong and were corrected against Ballotpedia and the candidates' own sites: "Justin Earley" -> Justin Early (TX-31 D) and "Jace Yarborough" -> Jace Yarbrough (TX-32 R). (4) Three nominees have no findable campaign website as of 2026-08-17 — Martha Fierro (TX-29 R), Eric Flores (TX-34 R) and Carlos De La Cruz (TX-35 R); all three are non-incumbents, so per contract they are recorded as rows with url and official_url blank, each with an FEC committee reference where one exists. (5) lauren4congress.com returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch, so its identity was confirmed from the indexed page title "Lauren B. Pena for Congress | Texas CD-37" plus a KVUE nomination race-call rather than a page read. (6) The unitedstates legislators CSV also truncated mid-file, yielding only 7 of the 11 needed bioguide IDs; the remaining four (Van Duyne V000134, Gill G000603, Sylvia Garcia G000587, Casar C001131) were taken from congress.gov member-page URLs. official_url is blank throughout because every incumbent in scope has a findable campaign site, making the house.gov fallback unnecessary. One search summary spuriously named a "James Kinney" as the TX-37 Republican; no source supported it and it was discarded rather than carried forward.

COMPLETE for scope: all 19 Texas districts (TX-01..TX-19) yielded both major-party general-election nominees, so 38 rows and zero exclusions. Every district had both a Republican and a Democratic nominee; none needed the "no major-party opponent" carve-out. 37 of 38 candidates have a verified campaign URL; the sole gap is TX-18 Republican Ronald Whitfield, recorded as a row with url and official_url blank per the non-incumbent rule (politics1 lists only a Facebook page for him, which I did not count as a campaign website). All 14 incumbents carry a bioguide id verified from a live congress.gov member URL, plus their house.gov official_url.

SYSTEMATIC OBSTACLE - the designated primary tracker of record was unreachable. Ballotpedia's "United States House of Representatives elections in Texas, 2026" page and its per-district pages returned empty bodies through WebFetch (JS-rendered/bot-gated), and direct browser navigation to ballotpedia.org was denied by the environment's navigation policy. I therefore substituted Wikipedia's "2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Texas" article as the nominee spine, fetched section-by-section via action=raw&section=N after confirming section indices through the MediaWiki parse API. Section-level fetching was necessary because whole-article fetches truncate: an early bulk fetch of districts 9-14 hallucinated around the truncation (it named Kay Granger, who left Congress in 2024, as the TX-12 incumbent, and hedged several nominees as "pending"). That output was discarded entirely and every district 1-19 was re-pulled at section granularity. Ballotpedia content did reach me indirectly and usefully via news.ballotpedia.org race-call posts surfaced in search results.

CORROBORATION - the two incumbent-defeat upsets were independently race-called as the contract requires: TX-02 (Steve Toth over Dan Crenshaw, Mar 3) via Ballotpedia News, CNN, NBC, The Hill and Houston Public Media; TX-18 (Christian Menefee over Al Green, May 26 runoff) via Ballotpedia News, NBC, CBS, Texas Tribune and Houston Public Media. Note two redistricting artifacts that would otherwise look like data errors: TX-09 is an effectively new seat with no incumbent because Al Green vacated it to run in the redrawn TX-18, and TX-18 was an incumbent-vs-incumbent Democratic primary. TX-08, TX-10 and TX-19 are open seats (Luttrell, McCaul, Arrington not seeking reelection).

NAME AND VERIFICATION CAVEATS - candidate_name follows the campaign site's own spelling where I fetched it, which diverges from tracker spellings in three cases flagged in notes: TX-09 R "Alexandra del Moral Mealer" (trackers say "Alex Mealer"), TX-12 D "Angela 'Heli' Rodriguez Prilliman" (politics1 says "Prillman"), TX-14 D "Thurman 'Bill' Bartie". Nine campaign sites were fetched directly and self-identified both candidate and district/office; the remaining sites rest on the contract's alternate prong, linkage from politics1.com/tx.htm, which supplied the bulk of URLs in a single retrieval. Two fetched sites (Jessica Steinmann TX-08, Tom Sell TX-19) named the candidate but did not state the district number in the retrieved homepage text, so their district attribution rests on politics1 tracker linkage rather than site self-identification. congress.gov itself returns 403 to WebFetch, so bioguide ids were read off congress.gov member URLs exposed in search results rather than from page bodies; this verification caught three errors in my prior recollection (Moran is M001224 not M001222, Self is S001224 not S001318, Fletcher is F000468 not F000472), so the ids here are source-checked rather than recalled. Scope note: the request mentioned NC/IL/OH primary timing, but SCOPE was limited to Texas 1-19 and only Texas was collected.

Full coverage: all 17 Illinois districts, both major-party general-election nominees each, 34 of 34 rows verified and zero exclusions. Illinois held its primary on March 17, 2026, and every district produced both a Democratic and a Republican nominee, so no "no major-party opponent" cases arose. Systematic obstacle worth flagging for the lane: Ballotpedia — the contract's primary tracker of record — was unreachable for this run. Every ballotpedia.org fetch (the statewide 2026 House page, the Illinois elections hub, and individual district pages) returned an empty body, and the browser pane hung for 300s on navigate, so no Ballotpedia page body was ever read; only Ballotpedia titles/snippets surfaced indirectly through search results, and those were not treated as confirmations. congress.gov was likewise 403 on its faceted member-search and state-listing URLs, so bioguide IDs were instead read off canonical congress.gov/member/<slug>/<BIOGUIDE> profile URLs surfaced by domain-restricted search — this caught one would-be error (Jonathan Jackson is J000309, not J000308). Substitute nomination evidence: the Wikipedia article "2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois," fetched section-by-section via action=raw so per-district primary vote tables (sourced to the Illinois State Board of Elections and FEC) were read directly, cross-checked candidate-for-candidate against politics1.com/il.htm; the two agree on all 34 nominees. Contested/upset races were additionally corroborated with news race calls: IL-07 (AP call for Koppie via WTOP/ABC News; Ford's Democratic win via Sun-Times/NBC Chicago), IL-09 (Elleson via Daily Northwestern and Journal Times; Biss via Sun-Times), and IL-04's unusual open-seat sequence (Chuy García's post-filing-deadline retirement and Patty García's sole-candidate nomination, via ABC7 Chicago, The Hill, and Fox News) — note a stale Ballotpedia snippet in search results still described Chuy García as a general-election candidate, which the news record contradicts and which was not used. Every recorded URL was fetched live on 2026-08-17 and confirmed to name the candidate plus the office/district; two redirects were followed to canonical hosts (melissabeanforillinois.com to melissabeanforcongress.com; lupe4congress.com to castillolupe.com). Nine sites do not print a party label on the homepage (Maxwell, Oakley, Conforti, J. Davis, Walter, Budzinski, Todd, Nolley, Vancil) — party for those rows comes from the primary-result source plus the politics1 tracker listing, never inferred from site tone. One row carries no site: Carl Lambrecht (IL-10, R), a non-incumbent for whom politics1 links only a personal LinkedIn profile; url and official_url are blank per contract. No official_url values were needed, since every incumbent had a findable campaign site. Residual soft spots for a later pass: the Donna Miller (IL-02) alternate domain godonnago.net could not be fetched (TLS chain error), and Jennifer Todd's site is at the .us TLD per Wikipedia while politics1 lists .com.

Complete coverage: all 14 North Carolina districts, both major-party general-election nominees in every one (28/28 rows, zero exclusions). Every district has both a D and an R nominee, so no "no major-party opponent" cases arose. All 13 incumbent bioguide IDs were read directly off congress.gov member-page URLs rather than recalled; this caught one error I would otherwise have carried (Valerie Foushee is F000477, not F000472). NC-11 has no incumbent on the ballot: Chuck Edwards (R) won the March 3 primary, withdrew in early August 2026 following a House Ethics matter, and the NCGOP executive committee installed state Rep. Jennifer Balkcom as replacement nominee on 2026-08-10 — corroborated by the NCGOP release plus NBC News, CBS News, and BPR/WFAE race coverage, per the contract's instruction to seek a news race-call where the tracker is ambiguous. Balkcom is the single row with no URL: nominated only seven days before this sweep, she has no findable campaign site as of 2026-08-17, and as a non-incumbent she gets both url and official_url blank. All other incumbents have live campaign sites, so per the contract's conditional phrasing official_url is left blank throughout rather than duplicating house.gov.

Systematic obstacles worth flagging for the lane. (1) Ballotpedia, the designated primary tracker of record, was effectively unusable directly — every WebFetch against a Ballotpedia page (state roster and per-district) returned an empty body, consistent with bot mitigation. I recovered Ballotpedia content only through search-result snippets, which was enough to confirm NC-08 and NC-14 but not to use it as the systematic backbone. Nominee verification therefore rests primarily on Wikipedia's 2026 NC House article fetched as raw wikitext, cross-checked against politics1.com and election2026.net, with news race-calls on the one contested/irregular race. If this lane depends on Ballotpedia as the tracker of record, that dependency needs revisiting. (2) The browser pane hung hard (get_page_text timed out at 30s, navigate at 300s) and was abandoned; 270towin returned 403. (3) Wikipedia's full-article fetch truncates before district 8, so districts 8-14 had to be pulled section-by-section via the parse API's section indices — worth reusing for TX/IL/OH tranches. (4) One retrieval actively produced wrong data: the unitedstates.github.io legislators CSV came back with stale/mixed rows (Ted Budd as an NC-13 representative, Ralph Norman under NC), so I discarded it entirely and verified IDs one at a time; do not trust that route in later tranches. (5) Three campaign sites (Hubbard NC-05, Ager NC-11, Barringer NC-13) return HTTP 403 to automated fetch and are recorded on politics1 linkage alone, which the contract permits but which is weaker evidence than the others. (6) politics1 proved reliable for coverage but not for link freshness — its LaKesha Womack link resolves to her consulting business rather than a campaign (corrected to womack4nc14.com), and it misspells Jamie Ager as "Agar"; five further politics1 links were stale-but-redirecting and were canonicalized to their live destinations. Names are spelled as the candidate's own site renders them where site and tracker disagreed.
